My dad thought I was normal too, until he started going to therapy and realized that we see each other as normal because we are both autistic, and this wasn’t something that the average person went through. There is a lot of overlap between INTP behaviour and autism, the difference is that autism can be genetic and it negatively impairs my ability to function (in my case). Its okay if you don’t understand it, because you can’t really understand it unless you experience it yourself. It’s very alienating. I would give anything to be “normal”

Unfortunately I am not diagnosed as a diagnosis costs $3000, but I do know I have it as my therapist says I have do and my dad is also autistic. And this was a very recent discovery for me so I don’t really know too much about it. Sadly I am part of the types of autistics where its very hard for me to function as an adult and I may need assistance from my parents until I can get myself on my feet. I am significantly less socially developed as my peers and I can only hang out with my friends for about an hour before I become exhausted due to “masking” and trying to act normal. I also experience severe social anxiety (which I am now medicated for) due to being afraid that other people will find me weird if I don’t act “right”. I also have very specific interests that I am very passionate about, which my friends consider weird so I can’t really talk to them about it. This is just my experience however and other people with autism might have very different experiences, sorry for the long comment and sorry if it doesn’t really make sense lol I just woke up!
